alignments.note: Anticipatory *it* for the extraposed infinitival subject the Hebrew writes; it denotes nothing the verse names and is `added` under rule 25's expletive sentence.
Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause takes the construction-supplied copula on the preposition, headed on the preposition (rule 49).
Substantival adjective with the indefinite article it licenses (rule 15).
No preposition stands before the infinitive construct, so the English infinitive marker *to* belongs to the infinitive's own unit (rule 52), headed on the lexical verb.
The waw already holds the *And* written for it and is not a home for a second connective (rule 51), and no other morpheme answers to *so*, so it is `added`; the ASV italic corroborates (rule 7).
Prepositional predicate takes the construction-supplied copula on the preposition (rule 49), discontinuous around the fronted subject under rule 25; headed on the word carrying the relation.
Construct noun with the indefinite article it licenses (rule 15).
The chain's *of* belongs to the *nomen rectum* (rule 19). The margin's *But a man of understanding hath wisdom* was read and set aside (rule 38).

review_notes: Two `added` units: the anticipatory *It* of the extraposed subject and the italic *so*, the waw already holding *And*.
The second colon's copula is placed on the predicate `לְ` under rule 49 rather than on the subject noun `חָכְמָה`.
